key_insight: Conformal prediction turns neural-operator CFD surrogates from deterministic predictors into calibrated, reliability-aware models for both vehicle-level drag and spatial surface-field uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: This enables aerodynamic designers to quickly prioritize which geometries or local surface regions need follow-up high-fidelity CFD verification, reducing wasted simulation effort.
method: Use GeoTransolver as the main surrogate backbone, with Transolver for transfer/architecture comparison.
Apply conformalized quantile regression for drag coefficient intervals.
For pressure and wall shear stress, combine point prediction with residual-scale estimation and residual-normalized conformal calibration at global, point-adaptive, and case-wise levels.
evidence_signal: On DrivAerML with 90% nominal coverage, out-of-fold calibration reduced Monte Carlo coverage standard deviation from 10.41 to 3.10 percentage points, and point-adaptive calibration cut mean interval width by 22.68% for pressure and 25.35%–27.09% for WSS.
watch_item: The method improves calibration, but its reliability still depends on score design, protocol choice, and the quality/representativeness of the DrivAerML training data when applied to new vehicle geometries.
paper_title: Multi-Granularity Conformal Prediction for Reliable Neural-Operator Automotive Aerodynamic Surrogates
